# vulnetix_quality_gate (Resource)

The tenant's quality gate: the checks every vulnetix scan in CI must pass. When a check is set here it overrides the matching scan flag; a check left out leaves the flag in charge. One per tenant.

Manages the `QualityGate` config kind through `/config/objects/QualityGate/{name}`. Applies are recorded with the provider's `manager`, so a GitOps `vulnetix config apply --prune` leaves this object alone.

The server merges: an argument removed from the configuration is no longer managed, and keeps its last value on the server. Destroying the resource deletes the object.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# The tenant's quality gate. There is one per tenant, so name is always
# "default" and can be left out.
resource "vulnetix_quality_gate" "default" {
  severity       = "high"
  exploits       = "active"
  block_malware  = true
  block_unpinned = true
  cooldown_days  = 7

  eol = {
    block = true
    severities = {
      next_quarter   = "skip"
      this_quarter   = "low"
      within_30_days = "high"
      retired        = "critical"
    }
  }

  sca_autofix = {
    strategy       = "safest"
    max_major_bump = 0
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `annotations` (Map of String) Free key/value notes for people and tools (`metadata.annotations`), such as a ticket link.
- `block_malware` (Boolean) Fail when a dependency is known malware. Overrides --block-malware.
- `block_unpinned` (Boolean) Fail on a dependency declared without a pinned version. Overrides --block-unpinned.
- `cooldown_days` (Number) Fail on a dependency version published fewer than this many days ago. Overrides --cooldown.
- `eol` (Attributes) End-of-life policy. A dependency whose product reaches end of life inside a horizon is reported at that horizon's severity, and blocks when it meets the gate. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--eol))
- `exploits` (String) Fail on a vulnerability with an exploit at or beyond this maturity. Overrides --exploits. One of `poc`, `active`, `weaponized`.
- `labels` (Map of String) Free key/value labels (`metadata.labels`). Stored with the object, never interpreted by the server.
- `name` (String) The object's name. QualityGate is one per tenant, so it is always `default`.
- `sca_autofix` (Attributes) How vulnetix fix and scan --sca-autofix choose a target version. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--sca_autofix))
- `severity` (String) Fail on any affected vulnerability at or above this severity. Overrides --severity. One of `low`, `medium`, `high`, `critical`.
- `version_lag` (Number) Fail on a dependency more than this many releases behind the newest. Overrides --version-lag.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The object's name, the same as `name`.

<a id="nestedatt--eol"></a>
### Nested Schema for `eol`

Optional:

- `block` (Boolean) Fail on end-of-life dependencies at all. Overrides --block-eol. The horizon severities are only read when this is true.
- `severities` (Attributes) The severity given to a dependency by how close its end of life is. skip ignores that horizon. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--eol--severities))

<a id="nestedatt--eol--severities"></a>
### Nested Schema for `eol.severities`

Optional:

- `next_quarter` (String) One of `skip`, `low`, `medium`, `high`, `critical`. Schema default: `low`.
- `retired` (String) One of `skip`, `low`, `medium`, `high`, `critical`. Schema default: `critical`.
- `this_quarter` (String) One of `skip`, `low`, `medium`, `high`, `critical`. Schema default: `medium`.
- `within_30_days` (String) One of `skip`, `low`, `medium`, `high`, `critical`. Schema default: `high`.



<a id="nestedatt--sca_autofix"></a>
### Nested Schema for `sca_autofix`

Optional:

- `max_major_bump` (Number) The most major versions a fix may jump. 0 keeps fixes within the current major.
- `strategy` (String) latest: the newest release. safest: the release with the fewest known vulnerabilities. stable: the newest release past its cooldown. rolling: the newest release that is not malware, known vulnerabilities allowed. One of `latest`, `safest`, `stable`, `rolling`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = vulnetix_quality_gate.default
  id = "default"
}
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# A config object is imported by its name. QualityGate is always "default".
terraform import vulnetix_quality_gate.default default
```
